claim: Botassart's Tombeau du Géant is classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia' with free 24/7 access and a refreshment bar/restrooms in July-August.
quote: The Giant's Tomb is an exceptional geomorphosite classified as 'exceptional heritage of Wallonia'... Free access all year round, 7 days a week, 24/7, and refreshment bar and restrooms are available in high season (July-August).

claim: The Botassart viewpoint offers a plunging view of the Semois meander winding around a wooded promontory.
quote: The Botassart viewpoint offers a plunging view of the meander, showcasing the Semois making the most of the relief, constantly winding back and forth.

claim: The Rochehaut panorama over Frahan stretches along 300m of road with a balustrade and free binoculars, classified as a major heritage site of Wallonia.
quote: The viewpoint is arranged along 300 meters of length, along the asphalt road, and impresses with the expansiveness of the landscape opening to viewers. There is a balustrade with free binoculars.

claim: The Frahan viewpoint has been classified as a 'Jewel of Wallonia' since 2015 and is one of the most photographed viewpoints in Belgium.
quote: The site has been classified as a 'Jewel of Wallonia' since 2015 and has become one of the most photographed viewpoints in Belgium.

claim: The Frahan loop trail from Laviot through the Vallée de la Semois National Park is about 9.5 km with 300 m elevation gain, taking 2.5-3 hours.
quote: The Frahan Loop starts in Laviot and takes you through the Vallée de la Semois National Park, following the river to the Corbeaux viewpoint and the village of Frahan. This loop covers 5.9 miles with an elevation gain of 1,000 feet

claim: The Semois Tobacco Route is a two-circuit driving itinerary across Vresse and Bouillon communes highlighting the tobacco-growing heritage that shaped the valley for over a century.
quote: The Semois Tobacco Route is a circuit made up of 2 routes to be followed by car in the communes of Vresse and Bouillon, aiming to highlight the last witnesses of tobacco growing

claim: Vresse-sur-Semois became a 'village of painters' in the early 20th century when José Chaidron founded the Vresse School around 1920; the former Hotel La Glycine now hosts the tourism office and art exhibitions.
quote: In the early 20th century, Vresse-sur-Semois became the village of painters, with José Chaidron founding the 'Vresse School' around 1920... Vresse-sur-Semois is known as a 'Village of Art,' with the former Hotel La Glycine serving as the local tourism office

claim: Laforêt was awarded the 'Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia' label on 7 October 1955 and remains one of the rare southern Ardenne villages to keep its original character.
quote: This label was awarded on October 7, 1955, and is well-deserved as Laforêt is one of the rare villages of southern Ardenne that has retained its former character.

claim: Laforêt's rustic Pont de Claies — woven hornbeam-branch panels on frail pillars in the river — is reopened each summer between mid-June and mid-September.
quote: Laforêt is famous for its illustrious 'Pont de Claies' on the Semois, a rustic bridge made up of panels woven with hornbeam branches placed on frail pillars in the riverbed itself. In summer, you can cross the famous 'Pont de Claies', which is reopened between mid-June and mid-September

claim: Alle-sur-Semois' Récréalle leisure complex has a 300-space private car park and free return mini-buses for kayak descents.
quote: The facility has a private parking area with 300 places, and free mini-buses are provided for your return trip when doing the Semois kayak descent.

claim: Top-rated Alle-sur-Semois attractions include Ardois'alle (a former slate-mine guided tour, 4.5/5) and Kayaks La Vanne (4.9/5), with Récréalle offering 7-27 km kayak descents plus bowling.
quote: Ardois'alle (4.5/5 stars) - A guided tour through a former slate mine... Kayaks La Vanne (4.9/5 stars)... Récréalle offers kayaking descent options (7, 12, 22, or 27 km routes along the Semois River), plus bowling and playground activities.

claim: The 52nd Festival des Arts de la rue at Chassepierre runs 15-16 August 2026 with 50+ street-arts companies from Belgium, France, Spain, Netherlands and Germany.
quote: Over two days, some of Europe's finest young artists, musicians, dancers and puppeteers entertain the crowds at the festival's beautiful riverside hub, on the banks of the pretty Semois river. Over 50 companies

claim: Chassepierre is one of the Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia, sitting on a rocky spur where the Semois 'is on stage'.
quote: Chassepierre, the Semois is on stage - Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia

claim: Mortehan's classified old cemetery, decommissioned in 1899 and listed as a historical monument in 1972, is the village's signature draw alongside its slate houses and old mill.
quote: The old cemetery in Mortehan carries visitors into another world... This cemetery was decommissioned in 1899 and was classified as a historical monument on November 20, 1972.

claim: Dohan (179 inhabitants) features an early-17th-century schist-and-sandstone castle on a rocky bluff and the Point de vue de la Schevauchée over its bridge.
quote: A castle was constructed in the early 17th century, presenting itself as an imposing manor in schist and sandstone partially rendered, built on a rocky foundation dominating the Semois about twenty meters high... The most prominent viewpoint is the Point de vue de la Schevauchée

claim: Poupehan sits in one of the most spectacular Semois meanders and is the access point for Les Échelles de Rochehaut — a steep ladder-equipped trail along schist cliffs.
quote: Poupehan is nestled in one of the most spectacular meanders of the Semois... Les Échelles de Rochehaut (The Ladders of Rochehaut) is a dizzying trail equipped with metal ladders, climbing up the side of schist cliffs, accessible from Poupehan via the GR16.

claim: Membre-sur-Semois is reached by a family-friendly 3-hour Alle-Membre kayak descent featuring grey herons, beaver dam sites and the Jambon Belvedere Corten-steel platform.
quote: Arrival in Membre-sur-Semois, a picturesque village with a view of the Jambon Belvedere (Corten steel platform)... The Alle-Membre route takes 3 hours, is ideal with the family

claim: Parking in Bouillon is free citywide but fills up during peak-season weekends and major events like the Fête Médiévale and Fête de la Chasse.
quote: Only during top events (e.g. Hunting Festival - Fête de la Chasse, the Medieval Festival - Fête Médiévale) and on weekends during the real high season it is difficult to find a parking space. However, parking is free in the entire city.
